title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 14° ('Relation with generalized Jacobians') moves the torsor and Fermat-tower discussion of the preceding pages (in the elliptic case, p.720) back to the basic curve U = U_{0,3} = P^1_Z − {0,1,∞} over S_0 = Spec Z.

(1) J* is the generalized Jacobian (Rosenlicht–Serre) of U, i.e. of P^1_Z with the reduced modulus m = 0+1+∞. It is the group of divisors on U modulo div(f) with f ≡ 1 at 0, 1, ∞. It is a commutative group scheme over Z, fitting into (305): 1 → J^0 → J* →(deg) Z_{S_0} → 1.

(2) J^0 is the rank-2 split torus G_m ⊗_Z M. A degree-0 divisor div(f) maps to (f(0), f(1), f(∞)) mod scalars, so J^0 ≅ G_m^{{0,1,∞}}/diag. The next page also writes it as Ker(product: G_m^3 → G_m).

(3) There is a canonical Abel–Jacobi morphism (306) φ: U → J^1, where J^1 = deg^{-1}(1) is a J^0-torsor.

(4) The anharmonic group S_3 acts on U by permuting {0,1,∞}. By functoriality it acts on J*, compatibly with (305), and φ is S_3-equivariant. Hence J^1 is an (S_3, J^0)-torsor, classified by the equivariant cohomology group H^1(S_0, S_3; J^0).

(5) Next page: Grothendieck claims H^0 = H^1 = 0. Consequently J^1 has a unique S_3-invariant section over Z, even though U itself has no S_3-fixed Z-point (the fixed points are the primitive 6th roots of unity). This gives a canonical S_3-equivariant identification J^1 ≅ J^0, and so a canonical S_3-equivariant morphism U → T = G_m^2 over Z.

(6) That morphism is essentially t ↦ (t, 1−t) up to signs. It is the 'unit-equation' embedding of U into a 2-dimensional torus. Pulling back the n-isogenies of T along it gives the Fermat curves x^n + y^n = 1. The Tate module T_∞(J^0) = Ẑ(1)^2 is π_1^{ab}(U). So the 'Fermat torsors' asked about on p.720 become, for U_{0,3}, pullbacks of the torsors T_∞(J^0)/[n].

The purpose is to describe the Fermat (maximal abelian) tower of U_{0,3} canonically over Z, with its S_3-symmetry. This prepares a comparison with the elliptic case on the previous page.
errors: No genuine error on this page. There is a subtlety Grothendieck himself flags on the next page. G_m^3/diag (cocharacter lattice Z^3/Z, a weight-type lattice) and Ker(product) (sum-zero, root-type lattice) are isomorphic tori. The isomorphism (x0,x1,x∞) ↦ (x1/x∞, x∞/x0, x0/x1) is only A_3-equivariant; transpositions act through an extra inversion, i.e. a sign twist. The two S_3-modules differ by the sign character.

The twist is harmless for the vanishing claims. In both versions J^0(Z) ≅ (Z/2)^2 is the 2-dimensional irreducible (Steinberg) F_2[S_3]-module, and Pic(Spec Z) = H^1(Z, G_m) = 0. So H^0(S_3, J^0(Z)) = 0, since S_3 permutes the three non-trivial elements transitively. And H^1 = 0, since that module is projective (free over the Sylow 2-subgroup). Claim (307) is therefore correct, although the argument via the spectral sequence H^p(S_3, H^q(S, J^0)) is only begun on the next page.
The page leaves undefined the lattice written 'Z^M' (or M with a crossed-out subscript). From context it is the S_3-lattice of degree-0 divisors supported on {0,1,∞}, or its dual.

ideas.what: Generalized Jacobian of P^1 minus 0,1,∞ over Z as an extension of Z by a rank-2 torus, with Abel–Jacobi map U → J^1
ideas.modern_name: Rosenlicht–Serre generalized Jacobian with modulus 0+1+∞; Albanese/Abel–Jacobi map of a punctured curve; 1-motive [Z → G_m^2]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenlicht (1954), Serre (Groupes algébriques et corps de classes, 1959); relative versions Deligne (Hodge III, 1-motives)
ideas.where_published: Unsure; possibly parts of La Longue Marche (1981, circulated). Not in EGA/SGA in this form.

ideas.what: S_3-equivariant torsor J^1 classified by equivariant cohomology H^1(Spec Z, S_3; J^0), shown to vanish, giving a canonical S_3-invariant base point and a canonical equivariant map U_{0,3} → G_m^2 over Z
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant (Grothendieck/Tohoku) cohomology of a group acting on a scheme; rigidification of the Abel–Jacobi map; S_3-symmetric unit-equation embedding
ideas.usually_credited_to: Equivariant cohomology: Grothendieck (Tohoku 1957). The symmetric embedding is folklore (Ihara, Deligne, Anderson on Fermat curves).
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts as far as known; the general framework is in the Tohoku paper.

ideas.what: Using the generalized Jacobian to produce the Fermat tower and abelian torsors of U_{0,3}; T_∞(J^0) = π_1^ab
ideas.modern_name: Fermat tower as pullback of torus isogenies; maximal abelian pro-cover of P^1 − 3 points; Ihara's power series / Anderson–Ihara
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Annals 1986, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'); Anderson; Deligne (1989)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions Fermat curves and the anabelian setting only in general terms; details unsure.

missed.claim: Over Spec Z, the degree-1 component J^1 of the generalized Jacobian of P^1 − {0,1,∞} has a unique S_3-invariant section. The reason is H^0 = H^1 = 0 in S_3-equivariant cohomology, which rests on the projectivity of the 2-dimensional F_2[S_3]-module J^0(Z). This yields a canonical, fully S_3-equivariant Abel–Jacobi embedding U_{0,3} → G_m^2 over Z, although U has no S_3-fixed Z-point.
missed.quote: Notons que J^1 est un J^0-torseur et [même un (S_3, J^0)-torseur ... (307) H^0(S_0,S_3,J^0) = H^1(S_0,S_3,J^0) = 0]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a small but clean rigidification statement, useful for S_3-equivariant normalizations of Ihara's universal power series, Fermat-tower Galois representations and polylog/Kummer cocycles over Z. It is usually handled by ad hoc choices of tangential base points. It is not deep, and specialists would find it plausible.

missed.claim: The page treats the elliptic-curve 'Fermat torsors' of the previous page and the U_{0,3} case uniformly, as torsors under T_∞ of a generalized Jacobian equipped with an Abel–Jacobi map. This suggests a common 1-motive framework for abelian towers of both hyperbolic curve types U_{0,3} and U_{1,1}.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor organizing viewpoint. The 1-motive language (Deligne) makes it standard now, so novelty is low.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard: the generalized Jacobian of P^1 minus 3 points and the Fermat tower via torus isogenies. The only non-routine touch is the S_3-equivariant cohomology argument giving a canonical invariant base point over Z. It is correct and neat, but small and easily rediscovered.
transcription_corrections: 'J^0 ≃ G_m ⊗ Z^M [?]' is more likely 'J^0 ≃ G_{m,S_0} ⊗_Z M' (with a crossed-out subscript on M), consistent with (308) on the next page.
'quasi-quot[?]' is illegible. The word after 'J* = J*,' and continuing onto the next line seems to end in '-quant ... vers Z', perhaps 'quasi-compact' or 'représentant'. Uncertain.
The marginal insertion '{U_{0,3} =}' is a correction rewriting U_{0,3,Z} as U_{0,3} after deleting the Z subscripts. The deleted strikeouts are Z subscripts, not P_Z.
The '145' in the lower left is archive pagination; the author's own page number is presumably 720 bis or similar (not visible).
